title: Fix: SNAT affinity break during dedicated route reparenting causing transient cross-tenant egress/DNS leakage
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Several Dedicated customers reported intermittent connections from tenant workloads to other tenants' backend services during peering/route failover. Symptoms included short-lived successful TCP handshakes to a wrong backend IP and DNS responses resolving to unexpected private addresses for a few seconds after route updates. This ticket tracks investigation, root cause, mitigation, and a permanent fix.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Provision two tenant VPCs with a dedicated peering configuration (Tenant-A and Tenant-B) in the same region.
2) Deploy a long-lived client workload in Tenant-A that initiates outbound TCP connections to an external database via the tenant NAT (ephemeral source ports observed).
3) Trigger a controlled peering route reparenting event (simulate autoscaler moving gateway pods and reattaching routes).
4) Observe conntrack/SNAT table entries on the egress node and run tcpdump on both the tenant NAT and the upstream router during the swap.
5) Make repeated DNS lookups for an internal service behind Tenant-B's peering (split-horizon) during the failover window and monitor responses from the node-local resolver.
6) Reproduce intermittent cross-tenant responses: some TCP flows complete to Tenant-B endpoints and DNS cached a reply from external resolver leading to transient misresolution.
Notes: Repro depends on timing of conntrack expiration, SNAT port reuse, and parallel resolver fallback to an external stub during short windows when the split-horizon responder is reparenting.
root_cause: When peering routes reparent between gateway instances, we observed that per-tenant conntrack entries persisted with SNAT mappings tied to old egress interfaces. If the new gateway rewrites egress IPs and the ephemeral port was reused, replies from the upstream network could be accepted and associated with the wrong tenant namespace. Simultaneously, the node-local DNS forwarder fell back to an external resolver while the split-horizon daemon restarted, and its positive response was cached briefly. The combination of stale conntrack/SNAT mappings plus cached external DNS created a transient cross-tenant leak window.
fix_summary: Implemented a two-part fix: 1) control-plane change to explicitly quiesce and sweep per-tenant conntrack/SNAT state during gateway reparenting events; 2) make the node-local resolver prefer internal split-horizon answers and queue queries during split-horizon agent restart instead of failing open to external resolvers. The conntrack sweep is implemented in the gateway agent (hotfix) and the resolver change is a small behaviour change in the node-local forwarder.
rollout_plan: Hotfix (canary): Deploy gateway-agent v2.3.1 to 5% of Dedicated clusters for 2 hours, observe conntrack sweep metrics and customer-reported errors dashboard.
Verify resolver behaviour: Deploy node-resolver v1.8.0 with 'fail-closed' split-horizon mode to canary clusters concurrently.
Full rollout: Ramp gateway-agent to 50% over 6 hours if canary shows no regressions, then 100% over the next 24 hours.
Rollback plan: Revert gateway-agent to v2.3.0 and node-resolver to v1.7.4 if we detect increased packet drops or DNS latency > 200ms sustained across >5% of clusters.
Post-rollout: Run synthetic tenant-isolation canaries in all regions for 48 hours and schedule a customer notification and postmortem.
test_plan: Unit tests for conntrack sweep logic and e2e tests that simulate route reparenting
Integration test: synthetic peering swap harness that validates no cross-tenant TCP completions when swaps occur under load
DNS test: force split-horizon agent restart and ensure resolver does not return external answers within 60s window for private hostnames
Load test: ensure sweep does not cause CPU spikes > 30% on gateway nodes at production scale
notes: Customer escalations came from two mid-market customers on dedicated reservations (support tickets #INC-2026-34 and #INC-2026-46). Both reported short (2-10s) windows of cross-tenant reachability after autoscaler-driven gateway move. Legal/compliance flagged potential PII exposure risk—triage marked high and security engaged.
communications: Support triaged and notified impacted customers with initial mitigation steps (manual gateway restart), CS lead scheduled weekly sync. Legal advised retention of packet captures for 90 days for affected tenants.
postmortem_actions: 1) Add automatic synthetic canaries to detect per-tenant SNAT reuse anomalies; 2) Add telemetry: conntrack sweep counts, resolver fallback rates, and per-tenant egress anomaly metric; 3) Update runbook and KB for Dedicated peering failover; 4) Schedule quarterly audit for resolver/split-horizon components.
